additional_concerns: All 12 required pairs are retained. NOT_APPLICABLE addresses only the typed trigger question; it does not authorize deleting these requirements from a broader compliance model.

Footnote 3 is supplied and marked on XML and PDF methods. The extractions' missing-footnote and unresolved-method statements are stale. Extending e-Cert to the unmarked web-form method is unsupported by this text.

The PDF permission is supported as a method choice subject to prescribed format and e-Cert. If its extracted conditions are treated as exhaustive sufficient conditions, they omit e-Cert. That extraction issue is separate from correspondence to a resubmission-trigger formula.

The date-only candidate includes pre-9:00am filings on 2 February 2026; the operational-launch candidates exclude them. The date-effective wording in u3 and launch wording in u11/u13 support competing temporal readings that should remain explicit. The predicates are not equivalent.

The governing timezone and exact inclusion of the launch instant are not expressly resolved. Authoritative clarification is absent, with no identifiable dependency mapping. Temporal uncertainty does not make the separate format or certificate claims unsupported.

The blackout provision permits urgent direct contact, not unrestricted alternative-channel submission. Contact alone does not establish submission; an actual submission made through contact should not be excluded merely because contact was involved.

node.29b224046d115582fbf223fb returns FALSE for a known non-submission within licensed-firm scope, whereas the other event candidates return OUT_OF_SCOPE. Their equivalence depends on whether non-submission inputs are admitted.

FALSE means no trigger under the assessed predicate, not compliant filing or permission to use another channel. Adding certificate or schema compliance as conditions of the other-channel trigger would require separate support.

The history candidate delegates event quantification, report identity and sufficient negative-history evidence to an external Boolean. Missing history must not become FALSE. Later resubmission does not erase an earlier trigger; these questions do not determine whether the duty remains outstanding.

Original-submitter and responsible-entity classifications may differ for agency filings or responsibility transfers. The circular does not resolve these cases; a submitter classification must not silently exclude filings on a licensed firm's behalf.

The XML passage also requires prompt liaison for a technical test. The atomic schema claim does not exhaust XML transition obligations, although that separate duty is outside the historical-trigger question.

The prescribed PDF specification, separately provided XML schema and promised JFIU resubmission guidance are absent. Guidance may clarify procedures or boundaries, but its issuance is not an express prerequisite to the duty. The four null-hash dependencies lack descriptions; no mapping or AVAILABLE finding is justified.
